the psychological contract is a dynamic construct, that the content of the contract is not fixed, that the contract can be renegotiated at any stage in the relationship, and that it is not only the individual who is responsible for the content of the psychological contract, but the organisation also plays a key role.

The main takeaway from our work is that
managers need to understand the nature of the psychological contracts they have with their employees and how those contracts affect knowledge‐sharing attitudes and behaviors.
